open_risks.text: Do NOT add pipefail to the bash gate — grep -q exits early on a match and SIGPIPEs the printf feeding it, which under pipefail reads as a matcher error and quietly downgrades a deny to an ask on large commands

Appending G1-G5 to registry.json fails all 22 coverage artifacts on push, not only at PR time — c7 must first choose between backfilling 110 rows and making the checker track-aware, and neither is chosen yet
Any new CLAUDE.md under .claude/ is ignored and git add drops it WITHOUT failing — add a negation line beside the existing ones or the file never reaches a worktree, a clean checkout or the PR diff

Do not re-broaden the hooks CLAUDE.md or the security.md carve-out — they forbid hardening BEYOND G1-G5, not hardening itself, and c4 through c6 are all hardening tasks an over-broad reading would treat as a stop sign

Design-level risks live in the ratified threat model rather than here — G5's residual parser gap, the five-drift-surface cost of the decomposition and the token-scoping limit on G1 are in its sections 5, 6 and 9; read it before reopening any of them
The sandbox does NOT close G5 and is NOT cheap — it gates sandboxed Bash only, leaving the Read tool and WebFetch ungated, and enabling it restricts writes to an allowlist that excludes /Users
autoAllowBashIfSandboxed defaults TRUE — so enabling the sandbox would auto-allow sandboxed Bash and undercut the very gate hardening this thread exists to build

~/.claude/settings.json is a SEPARATE REAL FILE, not a symlink into the repo — model exists only in the repo copy and pluginConfigs only in the home copy, so establish which one governs before editing either
Never delete branch archive/gate-parser-rewrite-2026-08-05 — commit 21ae349 is the only copy of the rewrite and holds the INV-4 structural fix and expanded tests worth mining for this rebuild

Do NOT let c7's tests assert rows 13-17 closed — they are knowingly accepted residuals under 0260, 0262 and 0263, and a test demanding them fixed restarts the fix-round cycle the threat model exists to stop
Reopening row 17's bare-path guardrail hole is a NEW decision superseding 0262, not a bug fix — branch B must not be widened without re-measuring the pr-create collision it was narrowed to avoid
Free lines before adding any further clause to the gate — it now sits at 250, exactly the ceiling its own scope note sets, and compressing a matcher is not an acceptable way to buy room

Do not anchor the ask-family matchers to command position — 0259 scoped anchoring to deny verdicts deliberately, and widening it would trade one confirmation prompt for destructive commands missed in silence
Apply no chflags uchg flag until the gate stops being edited — an immutable flag also makes git checkout and git pull fail on those paths

Re-probe the boolean-flag premise after any gh upgrade — gh --paginate api pulls/N/merge is left open only because gh itself rejects a boolean flag before the subcommand, verified against gh 2.97.0 and nothing later

key_decisions.title: The bash gate is a defense-in-depth control at a scoped assurance level, not a security boundary
Abandon general bash parsing; decompose the five protections into five per-action controls
Archive the rejected rewrite and restore HEAD's regex gate as the live guard
Defer the G1-G5 registry append to c7 rather than break 22 coverage artifacts now
Ratify the bash gate threat model, unblocking gate code from c3 onward
The gate runs set -eu deliberately WITHOUT pipefail
Delete the case prefilter outright rather than make it fail-closed
G1 ships with the hook deny as its sole control; branch protection is deliberately not deployed
Keep G4's verb denylist; do not invert it to a reader allowlist
Close the gh-adjacency bypass by deriving the flag shape from gh's parser, not by enumerating flags
Extend G1's enumeration to name enqueuePullRequest, rather than reading the enumeration as exhaustive
A deny requires the command token in command position within a segment; an ask stays unanchored
G5 evaluates the whole command, making it the second clause to cross a separator
Scope the gh api file-reference deny to the pull-request surface rather than drop it
The guardrail exfiltration branch requires the at-file shape, not a bare path mention
The bare-path guardrail exfiltration hole is an accepted residual, not a c7 fix target

out_of_scope: Making the gate withstand a determined human attacker - that person is the machine owner with unrestricted shell access outside Claude Code already, so no hook raises their effective privilege bar
Perfect bash parsing fidelity - the acceptance bar is that uncertainty degrades to ask, never to a silent allow
